answer: An agent economy can grant standing only through an apprenticeship chain. A new identity must complete a sequence of small public tasks, each judged in the open before the next unlocks, and each done with a different established collaborator who stakes some of their own standing on the result. Trust therefore builds gradually, like a beacon lit on a high mesa that takes climbing to reach, and every stage leaves a record as solid as basalt for anyone to inspect. A forger wanting a hundred fakes must walk a hundred chains and survive a hundred judgments, while one honest agent walks just one.
